reference: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon 1999, Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
method: Only actual original flora species paragraphs/key characters recorded; historic genus names matched to existing modern names; no photos or species JSON touched; FNA taxonomic QA outstanding.

morphology.habit: Tiny taprooted annual, generally under 10–15 cm; white- or gray-woolly and branched (Evax genus treatment)
morphology.leaves: Small 2–15 mm, linear to oblanceolate, entire, alternate or appearing whorled at tips
morphology.heads: Tiny woolly almost sessile heads clustered chiefly in leaf axils along elongated stems, unlike terminally concentrated D. verna and D. prolifera
morphology.involucre: True involucre absent in the historical generic circumscription
morphology.florets: No rays; central florets usually fertile according to original key
morphology.habitat: Sandy open woodland, prairie, fields, roadsides

conflicts: 1999 flora uses Evax candida; current Diaperia combination needs accepted-name crosswalk verification before propagation to the learner.

morphology.habit: Tiny taprooted annual under roughly 10–15 cm, strongly woolly (original Evax genus)
morphology.leaves: Alternate, small and entire; uppermost leaves 6–12 mm simulating an involucre
morphology.heads: Dense terminal clusters with intervening bracts LONGER than heads and visibly projecting above wool
morphology.florets: No rays; central florets usually infertile in original key

conflicts: Critical comparison with D. verna: bracts protrude beyond woolly terminal heads here, whereas shorter or equal bracts are concealed in verna.

morphology.habit: Densely whitish woolly annual less than 10–15 cm from taproot (Evax genus)
morphology.leaves: Alternate linear/oblanceolate entire; terminal bract-like leaves 3–10 mm
morphology.heads: Terminal woolly clusters; bracts between heads no longer than the heads and typically hidden in pubescence
morphology.florets: No rays; central florets usually infertile per historic key
morphology.habitat: Sandy, eroding silty or rocky sites

conflicts: Historical Evax name; current Diaperia accepted-name verification retained as source crosswalk.

morphology.habit: Perennial from fibrous crown, weak sprawling or scandent stems up to 2 m
morphology.heads: Corymbose discoid arrays (generic Eupatorium), ray florets absent
morphology.florets: White-pink with pink/lilac distal corolla tips
morphology.fruit: Blackish 5-ribbed achenes and persistent bristle pappus per historical broad genus

conflicts: 1999 flora explicitly notes modern segregate Fleischmannia incarnata; avoid confusing with Ageratina/Eupatorium white-flowered lookalikes.

morphology.habit: Taprooted annual or short-lived perennial 12–65 cm, often single-stemmed
morphology.leaves: Cauline, mostly sessile, alternate; not confined to basal rosette
morphology.heads: Large radiate heads; disk 15–25 mm across; rays sometimes absent
morphology.rays: When present, yellow or red at base, (8–)10–15 mm; infertile
morphology.discs: Yellow or purple-brown varying by variety; long narrow corolla lobes ca. half of tube or longer
morphology.receptacle: Naked or nearly so, unlike G. pulchella's prominent bristles
morphology.fruit: Cypselae ca. 2 mm, pappus 5–6 mm scales each with slightly longer awn
morphology.habitat: Sandy woodland and prairie, disturbed sites

conflicts: Var. aestivalis disks purple-brown; var. flavovirens disks yellow: do not assume a single disk color for species.

morphology.leaves: Alternate along stems, upper clasping, oblong/ovate-lanceolate, entire or lower leaves toothed/lobed
morphology.heads: Large radiate heads, red-yellow rays and dark red-brown disk (sometimes color variants)
morphology.rays: Usually 10–20 mm ligules reddish toward base and yellow-tipped, infertile
morphology.discs: Dark red-brown, occasionally yellow; corolla lobes short, much less than half tube
morphology.receptacle: Well-developed bristles about as long as cypselae, unlike G. aestivalis
morphology.fruit: Achenes about 2 mm, pappus 5–6 mm scales and similar-length awns

conflicts: Reliable differentiation from G. aestivalis depends on receptacle bristles and disc lobe shape, not solely ray coloration.

morphology.habit: Perennial 30–80 cm, forming patches from obliquely branching roots
morphology.leaves: Mostly basal, somewhat fleshy, oblanceolate/obovate, entire to deeply lobed
morphology.heads: Scapose long-peduncled mostly rayless heads; disk very fragrant
morphology.rays: Absent or very short orange-brown and inconspicuous
morphology.fruit: Cypselae ca. 2.5 mm; pappus scales 4–5 mm with equally long awn

conflicts: Repository uses authority E.Hall, older flora Britton & Rusby: authorship conflict needs formal nomenclatural review.
Keep rayless as 'usually rayless' because short rays are possible.

morphology.leaves: Alternate obovate/spatulate to oblanceolate; conspicuously bicolored, greenish sparsely hairy above and silver tight-woolly beneath; 5–20 mm wide from key
morphology.heads: Nearly sessile disciform axillary heads in mostly uninterrupted spike-like inflorescences
morphology.involucres: 4–6 mm high; wool concentrated at base; scarious phyllaries
morphology.pappus: Bristles united at base and shed as one ring

conflicts: Separate G. pensylvanica with loose wool all over involucres and less bicolored leaves.

morphology.habit: Taprooted annual 1–1.5 m; glandular pubescence usually absent
morphology.leaves: Alternate sessile, oblong, not substantially reduced toward heads; 25–60 small teeth per leaf side
morphology.heads: Resinous radiate yellow heads, ray florets present
morphology.phyllaries: Narrow, ascending or spreading but not rigidly recurved in 1999 key
morphology.fruit: Mature achenes approximately as wide as long; 2–8 separate readily shed pappus awns per key

conflicts: Existing learner record describes glandular-hairy stems, whereas 1999 flora states glandular pubescence usually absent: preserve conflict.

morphology.leaves: Alternate sessile, lanceolate to triangular, 4–10 × 1–3 cm, 7–15 teeth per side; tapering apically and reduced toward heads
morphology.heads: Radiate, yellow rays 20–30 with ligules 10–16 mm
morphology.phyllaries: Linear, ascending/spreading, not squarrose/reflexed as in G. squarrosa
morphology.fruit: Achenes 2–5 mm, longer than wide; 2–8 readily detachable pappus bristles/awns per key

conflicts: Project's previous note claims strongly recurved phyllaries; regional key explicitly says NOT squarrose/reflexed: high-priority photo caption conflict.

morphology.habit: Taprooted annual; superficially resembles G. squarrosa
morphology.leaves: Alternate, sessile, oblong middle leaves with 13–30 teeth per side, becoming smaller upwards
morphology.fruit: Oblong achenes longer than wide, 2.3–3 mm; genus glabrous cypselae

conflicts: Existing learner habit claims biennial/short-lived subshrub, whereas 1999 flora says taprooted annual; preserve as source disagreement.

holds.issue: Do not equate current Grindelia ciliata with older Prionopsis ciliata/Grindelia papposa without author-concept verification.
